title: Top K Frequent Elements
question: Given an integer array, how would you find the k most frequent elements? Compare different approaches and their time complexities.

rubric.name: problem_clarification
rubric.description: Asks about value ranges, k bound relative to unique elements, and tie-breaking requirements.

rubric.name: algorithmic_tradeoffs
rubric.description: Compares Hash Map + Min-Heap O(N log k) vs Bucket Sort O(N) approaches clearly.

rubric.name: time_space_complexity
rubric.description: Correctly states frequency map building O(N), heap operations O(N log k), and space O(N).

rubric.name: edge_case_handling
rubric.description: Handles k equal to unique count, k=1, and empty/single-element arrays.

rubric.name: communication_clarity
rubric.description: Explains why a min-heap of size k is preferable to sorting all elements O(N log N).

expected_signals: Identifies frequency counting via HashMap as mandatory first step
Uses Min-Heap of size K to maintain top K elements efficiently
Proposes Bucket Sort (frequency indexing) for linear O(N) time optimization
red_flags: Sorts the entire N elements costing O(N log N) without mentioning heap or bucket sort
Uses Max-Heap of size N costing extra memory and unnecessary log N operations
Forgets to account for HashMap creation overhead in time complexity
follow_up_prompts: Under what memory constraints would Bucket Sort become less attractive than a size-K Min-Heap?
How would you handle a streaming input where new elements arrive continuously?
